name: Tree
description:
The navigation tree (a sidebar's records grouped by owner). Groups collapse; leaf rows
are fa-item rows, two lines with a description, with an optional status dot on the icon. Keyboard: ↑ ↓ move,
→ opens or enters a group, ← closes or returns to the parent, Home / End, Enter selects
(toggles a group), and typing jumps to the next matching name. One row is tabbable (roving
tabindex). Rows are virtualised, so thousands of rows cost only the rows on screen.

With `selectableGroups` a branch is selected like a leaf and opens from its chevron. Large
trees load lazily: `hasChildren` marks a branch whose children `onLoadChildren` fetches on
first open, and `hasMore` with `onLoadMore` pages them in.

Opt in to multi-select with `selectionMode`, to reordering with `onMove`, to renaming with
`onRename` and to trailing content with `renderTrailing`; `ref` gives `reveal`. All of them
work on ids and the rows on screen, never by walking every node.
signature: ({ nodes, selectedId: selectedIdProp, defaultSelectedId, onSelectedIdChange, renderLink, rowWrapper, renderContent, expanded: expandedProp, defaultExpanded, onExpandedChange, query, emptyText: emptyTextProp, selectableGroups, onLoadChildren, onLoadMore, groupCounts, className, "aria-label": label, selectionMode, selectedIds: selectedIdsProp, defaultSelectedIds, onSelectedIdsChange, selectionLimit, checkboxes, renderTrailing, trailingVisibility, onRename, renamingId: renamingIdProp, defaultRenamingId, onRenamingIdChange, onMove, canMove, dragType, ref, }: TreeProps): import("react").JSX.Element

props.name: aria-label
props.description: Names the tree: "Endpoints".

props.name: canMove
props.description: Refuse a move: return false, or a sentence saying why. A row never moves into itself.

props.name: checkboxes
props.description: Show a check mark on each selectable row in `multiple` mode, which toggles it: the route on touch.

props.name: className
props.description: Classes applied to the outer element for layout. Use the component props and theme tokens for its appearance.

props.name: defaultExpanded
props.description: Initially expanded nodes when expansion is uncontrolled.

props.name: defaultRenamingId
props.description: The row being renamed at first.

props.name: defaultSelectedId
props.description: The row selected at first when the selection is uncontrolled.

props.name: defaultSelectedIds
props.description: The rows selected at first when uncontrolled.

props.name: dragType
props.description: What dragged rows carry, for a DropZone outside the tree. Default `TREE_DRAG_TYPE`.

props.name: emptyText
props.description: The line shown when nothing matches. Default: No match for “query”.

props.name: expanded
props.description: Open groups. Uncontrolled with `defaultExpanded`.

props.name: groupCounts
props.description:
Show each group's count of endpoints (leaves). Default true. Turn it off where a count
would mislead, such as an explorer whose branches are still loading. Lazily loaded and
paged branches never show one.

props.name: nodes
props.description: Graph or tree nodes with stable identifiers and relationships.

props.name: onExpandedChange
props.description: Called with the full list of open group ids whenever a group opens or closes (click, Enter, Space or the arrow keys); groups do not toggle while searching. Pair with `expanded` to control it.

props.name: onLoadChildren
props.description:
Load a branch's children the first time it opens (a node with `hasChildren` and no
`children`): update `nodes` with them, then resolve. A loading row shows meanwhile; a
rejection shows an error row whose Retry calls this again. Without it, the loading row
shows until `nodes` gives the branch its children.

props.name: onLoadMore
props.description: Load the next page of a branch's children (a node with `hasMore`): append them to `nodes`, then resolve. A rejection offers Retry.

props.name: onMove
props.description:
Makes rows movable: by drag on a pointer that hovers, Alt with the arrow keys (↑ ↓ among
siblings, reading direction into and out of a branch), and `TreeMoveItems` in a menu, the
single-pointer route (WCAG 2.5.7). A selected row moves with the selection. The host owns
the data: apply the move to `nodes`, with `moveTreeNodes` or on the server. Unavailable
while searching, when the rows shown are not the real order (R16.10).

props.name: onRename
props.type: ((id: string, label: string, details: TreeRenameDetails) => void | boolean | string | Promise<void | boolean | string>) | undefined
props.description:
Makes rows renamable in place: F2, or `TreeHandle.rename` from a menu. Enter or leaving
the field commits, Escape cancels. Update `nodes` to apply it. Return false, or a message
saying why, to stay in the field; a promise holds the field until it settles, and a
rejection says "Couldn't rename".

props.name: onRenamingIdChange
props.description: Called when renaming starts or ends.

props.name: onSelectedIdChange
props.type: ((id: string | null, details: SelectionChangeDetails<TreeNode>) => void) | undefined
props.description:
Called with the id of the row the person selects by click, Enter or Space, and details
whose `item` is the node: an endpoint (leaf), or a branch when branches are selectable.
Not for a group that toggles, a disabled row or the row already selected. A linked row
also navigates.

props.name: onSelectedIdsChange
props.description: Called with the whole selection after each change in `multiple` mode.

props.name: query
props.description:
Filter text from the search field above the tree. Matching branches open and the
match is highlighted.

props.name: ref
props.description: The tree's handle: {@link TreeHandle}.

props.name: renamingId
props.description: The row being renamed, or null. Controlled while defined.

props.name: renderContent
props.type: ((node: TreeNode, content: TreeRowContent) => ReactNode | null) | undefined
props.description:
Draw a row's content (after the chevron) yourself, e.g. an entity identity's row tier,
so a tree row is the same object as the entity's table cell and header. The row keeps
its own states (fa-item: hover, focus, selected) and height. Return null for the
default icon, label and description.

props.name: renderLink
props.type: ((node: TreeNode, props: TreeRowRenderProps) => ReactElement | null) | undefined

props.name: renderTrailing
props.description:
Content at the row's end: a badge, a size, a sync state. It may be anything, but the rows
are one tab stop (R11.5), so give a button `tabIndex={-1}` and repeat its action in
`rowWrapper`'s context menu. Clicking a control here does not select the row.

props.name: rowWrapper
props.description:
Wrap each row element, e.g. in ActionContextMenu so right-click, long-press, Shift+F10
and the Menu key open the row's actions (R11.6). Must render the row it is given.

props.name: selectableGroups
props.description:
Branches can be selected as well as opened (an explorer: a folder, a registry key). A
click, Enter or Space selects the row and fires `onSelectedIdChange`; the chevron, → and
←, or a double-click, open and close it. Per node with `TreeNode.selectable`.

props.name: selectedId
props.description: The selected row's id, or null for none. Controlled while defined; leave it undefined to use `defaultSelectedId`.

props.name: selectedIds
props.description: The selected rows in `multiple` mode. Controlled while defined.

props.name: selectionLimit
props.description: The most rows a range or Select All takes; the rest stay out and `details.limited` is true. Default none.

props.name: selectionMode
props.description:
`multiple` selects several rows (R11.8): a click replaces, ⌘/Ctrl-click toggles,
Shift-click takes a range. Keyboard: Space toggles, Shift with the arrows, Home or End
extends, ⌘/Ctrl+A selects all loaded rows. The selection is a list of ids, so it costs
nothing to hold and may name rows that are not loaded or are scrolled out of view.
`selectedId` keeps reporting the row last pressed without a modifier.

props.name: trailingVisibility
props.description: `hover` shows trailing content on hover, focus and selection, and always on touch (R11.7). Default `always`.
